description: Feed-driven GEX signal state machine. TWO data sources: Skylit Atlas (the page the panel runs on) and InsiderFinance (a second site read by a second userscript). Read session-state/INSIDERFINANCE.md before touching anything that consumes either.

canonicalFiles._howToRead: ⚠⚠ TIERED ON PURPOSE. The old flat list of 24 was read 'in full' — including a 607KB CHANGELOG and a 362KB CHAT-HISTORY. A context that reads everything reads nothing carefully. Read tier0 COMPLETELY and FIRST; it is small and it is the whole state of play. Then tier1. Tier2 is read PARTIALLY, per its own note. Tier3 is reference — do NOT read on load; open it when a task touches it.
canonicalFiles.tier0_note: These four are the state of play and total well under 100KB. LESSONS first: it names results that have been WITHDRAWN, and quoting a withdrawn number is the most expensive thing a fresh context can do because it looks like knowledge. OPEN-QUESTIONS stops you re-asking what he already answered.
canonicalFiles.tier1_note: The code and the facts that govern it. DATA-ARCHITECTURE is the ONE place that says who can reach what. FINDINGS is our evidence as against the Academy's prior.

tier2_readPartially.session-state/CHAT-HISTORY.md: 362KB. Read the CURRENT-CONTEXT entry IN FULL and nothing else. It is the only file carrying what was SAID rather than concluded — his corrections and his exact words.
tier2_readPartially.changelog/CHANGELOG.md: 607KB. Read the TOP ~5 version entries only. Everything older is archaeology; git has it if you need it.

canonicalFiles.tier3_note: ⚠ DO NOT READ ON LOAD. master-spec (2026-08-18), teaching-spec (2026-08-14) and skylit-docs/README (2026-08-14) predate the current design and are SUPERSEDED on data sources by design/DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md. Open one only when a task touches it, and prefer the code over any spec that disagrees with it.
canonicalFiles._projectFilesNote: ⚠⚠ DERIVED — the exact union of tier0+tier1+tier2+tier3, in that order. It exists because test_chat_history, test_em_band and test_futbars read it, and retiering without it broke all three. It is NOT a second list to maintain: test_lessons asserts projectFiles === the union of the tiers, so adding a file to a tier and forgetting this goes red. Add files to a TIER; never edit this by hand.

insiderFinance.payload: __NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.initialData  { ticker, tickerDetails, spot, options[], timestamp, isStale }
insiderFinance.formula: GEX = gamma * openInterest * 100 * spot^2 * 0.01, puts NEGATIVE
insiderFinance.verifiedAgainst: their published header, all expiries: ours call +263.83B / put -250.49B == page $263.8B / -$250.5B

windows.dte0: nearest expiry >= today. WARNING: their payload drops expired rows, so after the close dte0 is the NEXT session, not today
windows.toFri: today through Friday of this week; ROLLS to next Friday on a Friday (rolled:true)

insiderFinance.warning: NEVER compare a number from one window, book or scale against another. Four separate false-alarm bugs came from exactly that.

skylitApi.note: re-capture if older than ~30 days; the API is in limited beta

canonicalFiles.loadNote: Read session-state/PROJECT-CONSTANTS.md AND session-state/latest-resume-note.md BOTH — the constants file holds the failure patterns and the user's standing rules, the resume note holds only where we are. Then DECISIONS.md (why the panel is the way it is, D-1..D-13) and INSIDERFINANCE.md (the second book). ⚠ FRAME-APPROACH-REVIEW.md is a SNAPSHOT of 2026-08-23 — later builds closed some of its flaws without updating it, so verify every item against the code before calling it open.

loadCommand.instruction: When user invokes any of the aliases above, fetch ALL canonical files from the GitHub repository (rawUrlBase URLs), read the full userscript, read all Skylit platform docs, and report: (1) files loaded, (2) code architecture understanding, (3) platform understanding, (4) current version, (5) patch state, (6) next step. Do NOT ask for clarification on repo location — use the URLs above.

cloneRule.warning: ⚠⚠ CLONE FULL. NEVER --depth 1. This config said --depth 1 until 2026-08-27 and it cost the operator most of a session. latest-resume-note.md is REWRITTEN IN FULL every build, so every superseded note — and every locked item that silently fell out of one — exists ONLY in history. A shallow clone makes agreed, specified work structurally invisible. That is exactly how ITEM 18 (the Yahoo pipeline, locked 2026-08-16) was reported three times as 'never built' while its full spec sat in commit 72e820e.
beforeConcludingSomethingWasNeverBuilt: for c in $(git log --all --pretty=%h -- session-state/latest-resume-note.md); do git show $c:session-state/latest-resume-note.md | grep -qi "<term>" && echo $c; done

knownMissingAtHead.note: Referenced by this config, by the skill, or by live code comments, and ABSENT from the repo. Do not assume a fresh clone is broken; do not silently re-invent them either. ⚠ design/DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md WAS on this list and is now WRITTEN (2026-08-28) - it had never existed in any commit, verified with git log --all --diff-filter=A. skylit-docs/FINDINGS.md ALSO never existed and is now WRITTEN (2026-08-28) with F-1..F-8. ⚠ 2026-09-04: roadmap/ and archive/v15.53/ were on GitHub for the first time with v15.64 — both had been committed in the cloud and never carried by the installer (landmine L-Q, seventh directory). archive/v15.53/ is a RECONSTRUCTION from git bbd2f1a (tools/recover-archive.py; INDEX.md says so); the original per-block reasons are gone. The 26 retired tests live under archive/v15.53/tests/ and the installer deletes them from the operator's tree.

loadInstruction: ⚠ 2026-09-04 (v15.64): a fresh clone's suite is green but for the five permanent baseline files (test_expiry_profile · test_node_map · test_sma_cont · test_tapeking · test_v1126_process) and, until the day's records are committed, test_recordcurrent. If more is red, the installer did not run — the retired tests (archive/v15.53/tests/) may still sit at the root. roadmap/ROADMAP.md is GENERATED by tools/plan-seed.py; roadmap/PRODUCT-ROADMAP.md is stale (banner). ⚠ 2026-08-28: READ design/DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md - it is the ONE place that says WHO CAN REACH WHAT (the panel is @grant none and cannot fetch cross-origin; the companion holds the grants; the cloud can clone but CANNOT PUSH; git is the transport), every data source, the four transports, and the daily ES corpus pipeline. It exists because those facts used to live only in session-state/, which is rewritten in full every build - the same mechanism that lost ITEM 18 for 24 versions. design/architecture-design.md is SUPERSEDED on data sources by it. ⚠ TWO STANDING OPERATOR RULES, STATED HERE SO A LOAD CANNOT MISS THEM: (1) DELIVERY IS ONE FILE - see deliveryRule; send exactly one installvNNNN.bat and nothing else. (2) CHAT HISTORY IS REGENERATED ON EVERY BUILD and READ ON EVERY LOAD - see chatHistory; a build that skips it goes red on test_chat_history.js. ⚠ 2026-08-27: CLONE FULL (see cloneRule — never --depth 1). READ IN THIS ORDER, IN FULL, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: (1) session-state/latest-resume-note.md — a briefing, not a changelog; a context that skips it will re-litigate settled decisions. (2) session-state/CHAT-HISTORY.md, the CURRENT-CONTEXT entry — what was actually SAID last context: the corrections, the approaches already rejected, and the operator's exact words. The resume note says where we are; this says how we got there. (3) session-state/LOCKED-ITEMS.md — agreed work that is NOT built. It exists because the resume note lost ITEM 18 and a whole session went to re-discovering it. (4) design/DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md — who can reach what: the browser is the only participant that can fetch freely, the cloud cannot reach Yahoo and CANNOT PUSH, git is the transport between them. ⚠ master-spec.md §3.1-3.2 and design/architecture-design.md are OBSOLETE where they name AI Drive as the source of truth — both carry banners; git is the truth. TWO analyst packages inform the build (Garma = gamma-map-first, Wicks = charts-first); BUILD-PLAN.md is the master sequence across both, and is currently MISSING at HEAD. Several headline measurement rates in this project are ONE-DAY samples and at least one is contradicted by a later day — never quote a rate without its n and its date.

chatHistory.mandate: Operator-mandated 2026-08-27: 'everytime you make me a build i want this file updated with the chat history of the context. then when i start a new context you will feed the last context history to the new context also as a part of the load gex procedure.'
chatHistory.onLoad: READ THE CURRENT-CONTEXT ENTRY OF session-state/CHAT-HISTORY.md IN FULL, immediately after latest-resume-note.md and before anything else. It is the only file that carries what was SAID rather than what was concluded — the corrections, the approaches that were rejected, and the operator exact words. The resume note says where we are; CHAT-HISTORY.md says how we got there and what was already tried.
chatHistory.onBuild: python3 tools/chat-history.py --title '<what this context was about>', then fill DECISIONS / SHIPPED / OPEN AT CLOSE before committing. Generated from the real session transcript, never written from memory.
chatHistory.tiers: CURRENT CONTEXT is full detail; EARLIER CONTEXTS are compressed to the operator's verbatim prompts plus decisions. Each run demotes the previous current entry automatically, so the file stays bounded.
chatHistory.rule: Operator prompts are VERBATIM and are NEVER trimmed in either tier. Compression removes the assistant's replies only.
chatHistory.everyBuild: ⚠ REGENERATE session-state/CHAT-HISTORY.md ON EVERY BUILD - python3 tools/chat-history.py --title '<what this context was about>', then fill DECISIONS / SHIPPED / OPEN AT CLOSE by hand. test_chat_history.js FAILS THE BUILD if the version stamped in the history does not equal GPTS_VERSION, so a build that forgets it goes red. The operator must never have to ask whether this was done.

deliveryRule.rule: ONE FILE. Operator-mandated 2026-08-15, restated verbatim 2026-08-27: 'you are supposed to just give me an install file.'
deliveryRule.what: exactly one installvNNNN.bat (no dashes, no dots - downloads strip them), plus the Tampermonkey links pasted as text
deliveryRule.neverAlso: no zip+applier pair, no 'here are both options', no extra attachments sent alongside it
deliveryRule.fallback: gexdropNNNN.zip + applygexNNNN.bat are still BUILT and still work - send them ONLY if he reports the .bat failed
deliveryRule.howItBroke: tools/build-installer.py printed 'DELIVER THESE TWO FILES (primary)', PROJECT-CONSTANTS called that pair 'the primary delivery', and skills/gex/SKILL.md said 'ship ONE'. Three documents, two answers; a context followed the tool banner over the operator's standing rule and sent three attachments on 2026-08-27.
deliveryRule.enforcement: test_delivery.js fails the build if any source stops stating the one-file rule, if the builder reinstates a two-file banner, or if the builder stops printing the Tampermonkey links inside the delivery block.
deliveryRule.alwaysWith: ⚠ THE TAMPERMONKEY LINKS ARE PART OF THE DELIVERY, NOT A SEPARATE STEP. Operator-mandated 2026-08-24 and restated 2026-08-27: 'make sure you give me tampermonkey links when you give me install files.' Every message carrying an install file ends with the raw URL for the script(s) that CHANGED, plus: wait ~5 min for the CDN, CLICK THE LINK, reload Atlas.
deliveryRule.clickTheLink: Tampermonkey's default update check is ONCE A DAY, so a fresh push does not reach the browser on its own in any useful time. The click is the reliable step. A link offering 'Reinstall' means auto-update already won the race and he HAS the build - that is correct, not a failure. On 2026-08-27 a build shipped with no links and he ran a known-buggy version for an hour.
deliveryRule.howItReachesHim: (2026-09-04) When the session is LINKED TO HIS COMPUTER (mcp__remote-devices__* present): request C:\Dev\gex-signal-tapereader once, then device_commit_files the SAME installvNNNN.bat (fileUuid from SendUserFile) straight into that folder and tell him to double-click it there — no browser download at all. The Claude-in-Chrome side panel cannot hand a .bat to the OS ('This file type cannot be opened'), and downloads add ' (1)' copies; the repo folder is where he has always run them. Still send the card (SendUserFile) — it is the record and the fallback.
deliveryRule.extraction: (v15.64) the .bat copies its payload out with `for /f "usebackq skip=<HDRLINES> delims="` — NOT `more +N`, which walked 66,000 lines one at a time and sat on 'Extracting payload...' for minutes at 5.1 MB.

dataPipeline.summary: Companion v1.15 fetches Yahoo 1-min bars (ES/NQ/GC/CL) hourly -> gpts_futbars_v1 -> the panel carries them in data/YYYY-MM-DD.json under `futBars` -> the operator pushes -> tools/append-futures.py writes data/futures/<SYM>/YYYY-MM-DD.csv -> tools/study-hodlod.py rewrites BASERATES.json -> the companion couriers it back to gpts_hodlod_base_v1 -> the panel prefers it over the baked-in HODLOD_BASE. Only the two Yahoo legs are new.
dataPipeline.addAMarket: one row in FUT_MARKETS in current/gex-if-levels.user.js, e.g. { k:'NQ', y:'NQ=F' }
dataPipeline.ND: NOT ADDED. The operator named "nd" on 2026-08-28 and no context has identified the contract. test_futbars.js f26 fails the build if ND appears before he says what it is.
dataPipeline.blocker: data/es-1min/EPM26-1min.csv.gz is still not on GitHub (5.1MB vs a 6MB payload cap); until it lands the study cannot re-derive the 284-session rates.
dataPipeline.tape: (v15.66) THE WHOLE TAPE: every closed bar the panel captures SPXW's full velocity table (all strikes of today's expiry, Skylit's dollars + d5/d15/d60/d1d) and the whole Trinity ladders for SPY · QQQ · VIX (every strike as %King + the King's $K) into IndexedDB (repo.tape), and writes them ONCE at the close — the same 💾 / auto-export as the day file — as data/tape/<day>/<BOOK>.json (one shared strike list, one aligned row per bar). Not periodic (each write would be a 2 MB blob pushed by the sync task). Forward-only from v15.66; earlier days hold 8 SPY/QQQ strikes. Read with tools/nightly/tape.py; design/DATA-ARCHITECTURE.md §6b.

findings.onLoad: Read it with skylit-docs/learn/. The Academy is the vendor PRIOR; this is OUR evidence. F-4 is the one that changes behaviour: a 5-feature logistic was measured against a plain 2-axis lookup and added 0.0008 AUC on an identical Brier, so the TABLE ships. Do not rebuild the regression.

entries.F-1: the initial balance answers "is the extreme in"; sweeps do not (48%)
entries.F-2: a calibrated probability; momentum divergence adds nothing
entries.F-3: NQ cross-market divergence dead too (-0.0014); both only LOOK anti-predictive
entries.F-4: the model does not earn its complexity - SHIP THE TABLE
entries.F-5: there is still a trade left when the call fires (half the range ahead)
entries.F-6: red/green day is already answered by the open - do NOT build it
entries.F-7: the table transfers to NQ - one table serves both markets
entries.F-8: measure the question the FACE puts: 94% not 76%, 72% not 93%

lodhod.what: ⓪a: has the LOD/HOD already printed?
lodhod.engine: 8x9 lookup table, axes = posr (distance travelled off the extreme / running range) x 45-minute block. 284 sessions, 38,054 observations. NOT a regression - see FINDINGS F-4.
lodhod.thresholds: IN at cell>=70% (94% correct, median 09:55, n=284). NOT IN at cell<=20% (72% broke, median 09:45, n=85). Between them: STANDING.
lodhod.doNotQuote: 76% for the IN call or 93% for the NOT-IN call - both came from a sample that pooled BOTH sides at every bar, a question the panel never asks. See F-8.
lodhod.rejected: IB30/IB60/50-SMA/open-reclaimed/60m-breakout are proxies for posr; sweeps 48%; momentum divergence -0.0004; NQ divergence -0.0014; red/green adds nothing over the sign of price vs the open.
lodhod.status: PROVISIONAL - enrolled in FEATURES and learning/rules.json at n=0; the forward score is what turns it into a measured rate.

saveDone.rule: Operator-mandated 2026-08-28: EVERY message that delivers a build ends with an explicit "✅ SAVE DONE" line naming what was updated for a future context.
saveDone.quote: "after you give me a build, i want a confirmation something like a checkmark save done for future context. this tells me that you have updated the chat history and any relevant files that a future context would need to proceed if this context was closed."
mustBeCurrent: session-state/LOCKED-ITEMS.md (when an item opened or closed)
saveDone.enforcement: test_savedone.js fails the build when the resume note does not declare the current panel version, when CHAT-HISTORY or the CHANGELOG are unstamped, when a ledger is missing, or when this convention stops being written down. | test_lessons.js enforces session-state/LESSONS.md carrying the current version, as the TOP entry. | ⚠ test_recordcurrent.js keys on COMMITS, not versions: if a commit touched current/, tools/, session-state/, changelog/, data/, design/ or skylit-docs/, then CHAT-HISTORY.md and LESSONS.md must be from that commit or later. The version-keyed tests are BLIND to any work that does not bump the version, which is most of it - proven 2026-08-30 when three bodies of work landed under an already-recorded v14.88 and all three guards stayed green.
saveDone.why: latest-resume-note.md went SEVEN builds stale on 2026-08-28 and then FOUR more the same day, while CHAT-HISTORY.md stayed perfect - because a test guarded one and nothing guarded the other. A rule enforced by a test is followed; a rule enforced by a checklist is followed until it is busy.

farside.what: ⓪a's far-side block: P(a level trades before the close) x first-passage timing. v14.72.
farside.tables: data/es-1min/FARSIDE.json, derived by tools/study-farside.py, couriered by companion v1.16 into gpts_farside_v1 and VALIDATED before use (>=120 sessions, every rated cell n>=60, monotone in distance).
farside.evidence: FINDINGS F-12..F-16. F-14 is the model (AUC 0.826, calibrated); F-15 is the timing; F-13 says do NOT predict the far-side price directly; F-16 says the daily ATR and level identity add nothing - and records the phantom a sparse control produced.
farside.doNotRePropose: sweeps, momentum/NQ divergence, IB30/IB60, 50-SMA, open-reclaimed, 60m breakout, daily ATR, overnight range, volume, day-of-week, gap, prior-day/overnight level identity, red/green days, a 5-feature logistic, or a narrow high-probability timing window. All measured, all recorded.
farside.improvementLoop: the nightly review scores the touch call and the <=20% NO call, runs the gamma test with a DENSE distance control, and PROPOSES a new FARSIDE.json into review/ - it never applies one. See docs/LLM-NIGHTLY-BRIEF.md, the star section.
farside.⚠ correction: RESOLVED: HLTAB_META.inHit was corrected to 63 at v14.84 (F-12). This note previously said it 'still advertises 92%' and was stale from 2026-08-30 to 2026-08-31.

lessons.mandate: Operator-mandated 2026-08-30: 'i need you to either use a document you already have or create a lessons learned document which you update every time there is a build. You will then also make it a part of the load gex procedure so future contexts know the lessons.'
lessons.onLoad: READ session-state/LESSONS.md IN FULL, immediately after latest-resume-note.md and the CURRENT-CONTEXT entry of CHAT-HISTORY.md, and BEFORE proposing or measuring anything. Section 1 is the failure-pattern register - nearly every bug in this project is one of those patterns. Section 2 is the per-build log, newest first, and it names results that have been WITHDRAWN. Quoting a withdrawn number is the most expensive mistake a fresh context can make, because it looks like knowledge.
lessons.everyBuild: Add one entry for the shipped version. Write only: something that turned out to be FALSE that a future context would repeat; a failure-pattern recurrence WITH its concrete instance; or a measurement that superseded an earlier one, naming the number now withdrawn. If none: write the version and 'no new lesson'. NEVER delete an entry.
lessons.enforcement: test_lessons.js goes RED when LESSONS.md does not carry the current GPTS_VERSION, when this build is not the TOP entry, or when the file is dropped from canonicalFiles. A rule enforced by a test is followed; a rule enforced by a checklist is followed until it is busy.

loadSelfCheck.why: A load that reports 'files loaded' proves nothing was absorbed. Answer these from the files BEFORE doing any work, and say the answers out loud in the load report. A wrong answer here means the load failed and should be redone — that costs a minute; discovering it an hour in costs the session.

openQuestions.onLoad: Read it in full with tier0. It is the difference between asking him something new and re-asking something he already answered. An agent that re-asks is spending the one resource this project cannot regenerate.
openQuestions.everyBuild: Move anything answered into the ANSWERED section with its answer and date; add anything newly blocked. An entry leaves only by being answered or explicitly dropped.
openQuestions.rule: NEVER guess an answer and build on it. Print an em-dash, say why, and ask.

theWhatAndTheHow.process: design/DATA-ANALYSIS-PROCESS.md — THE DATA ANALYSIS PROCESS, named by the operator 2026-09-04: the seven links CAPTURE → ANALYSIS → TESTING → LEARNING → REC → DASHBOARD → SCORE, one definition end to end, the degrees of knowledge every face number carries, the ten rules, the eight tabs (the final set), the markets (learning/markets.json). His words: 'just click on the save button once a day probably eod, and from that point on you take over from data, analysis, testing, learning all the way to the Rec tab'. READ IT FIRST on load; test_data_analysis_process.js fails the suite if a link leaves it
theWhatAndTheHow.what: design/PURPOSE.md — find the HOD and the LOD early enough to trade the move between them; secondarily the pullback turning points that resume a trend; a gamma node deflects price and the deflection IS the turning point
theWhatAndTheHow.how: design/PROCESS.md — the loop RECORD → EXPORT → PUSH → NIGHTLY → REVIEW → REGISTRY → BUILD → INSTALL → GATE → DASHBOARD/THE READ → SCORE; Dashboard = act, Analysis = ask and read, Testing = trust and promote; every rate with its n; a scorer must be able to fail; hypotheses written before the data, read once at minN; every fetched file rides the installer; probe the live panel after every install
theWhatAndTheHow.dayLine: (v15.73) THE DAY LINE — the process reporting on itself at the bottom of the panel (dayLineState / dayLineHtml, .g3pline): the date, then saved · analysis · testing · learning · rec, each with its evidence (time, who, counts) and a colour (green done · amber expected, not yet · red overdue and why · grey not knowable). Sources: saveState / AUTOSAVE.lastWrite / DAY_WRITTEN, pipeLoad, ANALYSIS_NIGHTLY (the nightly log), learnLoad, recMerged — all already fetched on the 10-minute check. Overdue: analysis 30 min after the save with no log → red, names the GEX nightly task; a save not confirmed by 15:15 → red, points at the 💾 chip. Yesterday’s line stays until today records its first bar. Probe: __gptsDebug.dayLine(). Operator, 2026-09-05: "9/4 - data saved analysis complete, testing complete, recommendations made. something descriptive".
theWhatAndTheHow.rollingKing: (v15.72) HIS READ, REGISTERED BEFORE THE DATA: a King that rolled UP today and holds as a floor is the doctrine's rolling floor (bullish); rolled DOWN and holding as a ceiling, the rolling ceiling. Every tap is stamped with each book's King roll today (kroll); four classes in both twins — king:floor:up · king:floor:dn · king:ceil:dn · king:ceil:up (tapClasses / patterns.py tap_classes, pinned equal); K2.6 / K2.7 on Analysis; H8 / H9 in learning/register.json (pick pat, outcome resume, base dir:up / dir:dn, minN 30, since 2026-09-08, judgedBy nightly) read by run.py judge_pat from the pattern table. Nothing on the face until a class clears; then Rec proposes it. The face (v15.72): the AFTER HOURS bar at the bottom, the King cards on the whole row and bigger, the ladder 9 px, the leaked .g3pb border gone.
theWhatAndTheHow.autosave: (v15.71) THE SAVE RUNS ITSELF — no click at the close. Rule 1+2: after the close (15:01 CT and later, weekdays, no upper bound) any tick that finds the day not confirmed in the repo folder writes it (repoAutoExportTick → repoExportDay(TODAY,true,'auto')) and retries every 10 minutes until it lands. Rule 3: outside market hours every earlier day still in IndexedDB with bars and no file is written write-if-absent and marked once (repoLateSweep; kv dayWritten:<day>). SAVED means confirmed in the folder; the silent download fallback is gone. A timer may queryPermission but never requestPermission (v14.53): when the grant is missing the footer's 💾 shows DUE and his click carries the permission inside the gesture (repoClickExport; DATA_DIR_H cached at boot) — Chrome 122+ offers Allow on every visit there. Probe: __gptsDebug.autosave() (state · rules · written days · marketHours · afterClose); __gptsDebug.lateSweep(). The old auto-export stopped trying at 16:00 CT and wrote weekend files with no bars; both gone.
theWhatAndTheHow.rec: (v15.70) the 💡 Rec tab: proposals TO him — the nightly's rows (tools/nightly/recommend.py, pre-registered conditions) and the review's (tools/rec-seed.py) — in learning/recommendations.json; his ✓ / ✗ is saved in the panel (gpts_reco_v1), rides the day file as `reco`, and the nightly sets the row's status; a build marks a row IMPLEMENTED with its version (set status + version in rec-seed.py for the review's rows). Nothing on the face changes except through Rec.
theWhatAndTheHow.outcomes: (v15.69) every tap is scored on the two OBJECTIVE outcomes PURPOSE names — TURN (the tap's extreme within 0.50 SPY of the session's HOD/LOD) and RESUME (a new session extreme after the tap) — by tools/nightly/patterns.py from the day file's own bars, first tap per node per day; the nightly's pattern table carries them beside held (Testing ⑦, the Analysis rows' lines); the Learn tab's rules carry the record's verdict (results.py RULE_SOURCES: agrees / contradicts / thin / not measured) and the machine never changes a rule's status. First read F-19: turn 1 of 19 on 2026-09-03 — the base every class must beat.
theWhatAndTheHow.nightly: (v15.68) the nightly runs on HIS MACHINE: the 'GEX nightly' Windows task (setup-gex-nightly.bat once → tools/gex-nightly.bat every 10 minutes, hidden, no PowerShell) → tools/nightly/tick.py runs tools/nightly/run.py only when the newest day file is newer than its log → the log (ranOn 'his machine'), the pattern table, the tables, and the study registry the Analysis tab renders (tools/nightly/results.py → learning/results.json + studies.json patched: result · status · by:'nightly' · asOf; a thin row keeps the review's sentence) → the GEX sync task pushes it. The review (a session) owns the QUESTIONS in tools/studies-seed.py, which merges results.json so it never erases the machine's numbers. Never assume a session ran the nightly; read learning/log/<day>.json's ranOn.
